summary: Michela Clemente is a Tibetologist who studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and completed postdoctoral mentorship under Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015). She held a post at the University of Cambridge as a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellow.

Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin (~1853–1857) under Giacomo Lignana and Mario Vallauri. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1870) and was professor of philology and literature at the University of Naples Federico II (~1872–1914).
Michele Martin (born 1942) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and held a post at National Taiwan University.

Michelle C. Wang specializes in art history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She completed her doctoral studies under Eugene Y. Wang (~2002–2008) and served as assistant professor of art and art history at Georgetown University (~2012–2018).

Michelle Spuler (born 1971) specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Queensland (~1996–2000), taught at Colorado College, and taught religious studies at Victoria University of Wellington (~2001–2004).

Michiel de Vaan (born 1973) is a linguist working in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his doctorate under Alexander Lubotsky (~1997–2002) and held a post at Leiden University (~2002–2014).

Michihiko Komine (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1964–1976). He held posts at Taisho University (~1978; attested 2014–2015) and chaired the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies (~2015).

Michihiko Yajima (born 1963) is an Indologist and linguist who studied as a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981). He held positions at the University of Tokyo (attested 1992) and Tsurumi University (attested 2003–2008).

Michihiro Ikeda works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held appointments at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996), Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies as a librarian (attested 2005–2006).

Michiko Yusa (born 1951) works in religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She earned her PhD at UC Santa Barbara under Raimon Panikkar (~1976–1983) and served as a foreign languages professor at Western Washington University (~1983–2017).

Michio Kamikawa (born 1960) specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University (~1979–1988) and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University (attested 2016).

Michio Yano (born 1944) is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi and at Brown University under David Pingree (~1972–1974), later serving as professor at Kyoto Sangyo University (1973–2015).

Michitoshi Barada is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi, including at Savitribai Phule Pune University (1997). He held posts at Otani University (1992) and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (2000–2003).
Michiya Ito studied as a graduate student at Tohoku University (attested 1990) and later held posts at the same university (attested 1990, 2001–2004).
Michiyo Demoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Kyoto University and held an affiliation at the University of Marburg (attested 2024).
Michiyo Hoshi (born 1941) specializes in Tibetology and linguistics. She has held posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa and at Toyo Bunko (attested 2003).
Midori Nishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006) and later held a researcher post there (attested 2010–2015).
Mieko Kajihara specializes in Indology. She studied under Michael Witzel (attested 1997) and earned her PhD from Harvard University by 2002.

Migmar Tsering (1956–1999) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He served at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990) and headed Sakya College (attested 1991–1997).

Mihai Șora (1916–2023) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Bucharest under Mircea Eliade (~1934–1938), the University of Paris (~1939–1944), and the CNRS (~1945–1948). He worked at the State Publishing House for Literature and Arts (~1957–1969).
